description: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets published over time, categorized by researcher location, spanning the years 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "Year," and displays the years in chronological order. The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "Number of datasets," and uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^2, with major tick marks and horizontal grid lines at intervals of powers of ten (10^0, 10^1, 10^2). The chart features grouped vertical bars, where each group corresponds to a specific year. Within each year, the bars are arranged side-by-side to represent different researcher locations, as indicated by the legend titled "Researcher Location." The legend defines six categories with corresponding colors: Other (blue), USA (orange), IN (green), UK (red), IT (purple), and DE (brown). The number of datasets generally increases over time for most locations, with the shortest bars representing a value of approximately 1 (10^0), such as the USA in 2014, DE in 2015, IN in 2017, and IT in 2022. The tallest bar appears in the 2021 group for the "Other" category, reaching slightly above 10^2 (approximately 120). The "Other" category consistently displays the highest values from 2017 to 2021, while the USA category is present in almost every year, starting from approximately 2 in 2012 and peaking at around 45 in 2021. The groups are sorted chronologically along the horizontal axis, and the bars in the final year, 2022, are visually distinguished by being rendered in lighter, faded shades of their respective category colors.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of datasets over time for the five most frequent researcher locations and all other locations combined, spanning the years 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the years, while the vertical axis indicates the number of datasets on an exponential scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^2. Researchers from the USA consistently published the highest number of datasets across all years, with a peak in 2020. Notably, researchers from India surpassed those from the UK in dataset production in 2021, marking a significant shift in contributions. Additionally, the number of datasets from Germany declined steadily after 2018, indicating reduced activity in dataset production from this region.
